newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium arrests three in freezer murders.
newsitem.headline: Belgium arrests three in freezer murders.

text.p: Police have charged three Lebanese men with murder in Belgium's bodies-in-the-freezer triple killing, a prosecutor's office spokesman said on Monday.

He said Ghassan Bou-Ziab, 40, owner of the Baalbeck Lebanese restaurant where the bodies were found, and his brother Helmi Bou-Diab, 32, had confessed to killing their respective wives because they suspected them of adultery.

But, he said, they accused each other of killing another woman, who had not yet been formally identified but was believed to be their 70-year-old adoptive mother who lived in the apartment above the restaurant.

The third Lebanese man, Ronald Njaim, 25, was apparently involved in questioning the two wives about their alleged adultery in a confrontation which took place above the restaurant, the spokesman said.
The women were killed on August 18 but only put in freezers about six days later.
The bodies were found on September 3 by bailiffs coming to remove property from the restaurant, which closed suddenly last month.
The three men fled to the French city of Valenciennes last week but were arrested on Saturday on the Brussels-Mons motorway after returning to Belgium to turn themselves in.
The Baalbeck Restaurant lies in the heart of Brussels' diplomatic district and was well known among the international community for its good cooking.
